name: The Closing Prayer Incident
venue: Heritage Trust Inaugural Meeting, Mwisho wa Mwisho Community Hall
description: The elder invited to close the Heritage Trust's inaugural meeting in prayer prayed for 22 minutes. Three attendees departed before the amen. All three are recorded in the official minutes as present.
prose: The inaugural meeting of the Mwisho wa Mwisho District Heritage Trust was convened at the Community Hall on 3 March 1991 at 9:00 in the morning. Nine founding members were in attendance, representing three founding families. The meeting lasted three hours and fourteen minutes. It addressed the Trust's founding charter, the scope of its documentation mandate, its administrative structure, and the procedure for receiving incident submissions from community members. At approximately 12:14 in the afternoon, the proceedings moved to a closing prayer.

Elder Jeremiah Mwangi, invited by the presiding member to close the meeting in prayer, began at approximately 12:14 and concluded at 12:36. The prayer lasted twenty-two minutes. It addressed, among other matters, the Trust's founding purpose, the condition of the district, the health of several named community members, the success of the forthcoming harvest, and matters of a personal nature whose relevance to the Trust's mandate was not questioned at the time. For the first twelve minutes of the prayer, the nine founding members remained standing.

At a point between the twelfth and fourteenth minute of the prayer, three founding members — whose names appear in the official minutes of the inaugural meeting without any distinguishing annotation — departed the meeting room. Their departure was observed by the remaining attendees. No interruption was made to the prayer. The prayer continued and concluded without any acknowledgement of the departures. The amen was said at 12:36. The three members were not present to say it.

The official minutes of the inaugural meeting, recorded by the Trust's founding secretary, Mrs. Felicity Mwangi, record all nine founding members as present at the meeting. The three members who departed before the amen are listed without annotation, in the same manner as those who remained. All three have separately and individually confirmed, in testimonies collected by the Trust between 1992 and 1995, that they had left the room before the prayer concluded. None disputes that the prayer was still in progress when they left. Mrs. Mwangi has not provided a statement regarding the preparation of the minutes. This incident is the only one in the registry in which the documenting institution is itself implicated as a party.
heritageTrustNote: This is the only incident in the registry in which the Heritage Trust itself is implicated as a party to the discrepancy. The minutes were recorded by the Trust's founding secretary, who has not provided a statement. The Trust acknowledges the irregularity and considers it documented.

disputedAccount.summary: The official minutes record three individuals as present at the meeting's close. All three had departed before the amen was said.

accountA.text: Minutes read: "The meeting was closed in prayer and fellowship. All founding members in attendance." Three names follow, each of whom — by separate oral accounts — had left.

accountB.text: All three named individuals have separately confirmed that they had departed before the prayer concluded. None disputes that the prayer was still in progress when they left.
